self-concept of achievement does not significantly influence subsequent achievement in elementary school and that it makes a big difference whether achievement is measured by marks or tests.
self-concept of academic ability is a consequence of prior achievement, and not a cause.

the causal ordering of academic self-concept and school achievement in elementary school.
the causal ordering of the two variables self-concept of academic ability and academic achievement.
the question of how the causal ordering of academic self-concept and school achievement is influenced by the choice of the indicator for school achievement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-concept is not causally related to achievement during elementary school.
self-concept of mathematics ability and mathematics achievement are not reciprocally related during the elementary school period.
self-concept is a consequence of achievement, but achievement is not a consequence of self-concept in elementary school.

the skill development model is confirmed by our longitudinal data.
the self-concept of academic ability is not a cause, but rather a consequence of the students’ academic performance.

the causal ordering of academic self-concept and academic achievement is a question that needs to be addressed with multiple indicators of achievement.
